title: auth: unify header semantics for project/org keys, scoped tokens, nonce signing; OpenAI compat and streaming fixes
author: Ava Martinez
description: Motivation: We have several client integrations and the OpenAI compatibility layer that expect different header semantics for project and organization keys. There have been recent incidents where streaming sessions started before auth context was fully validated which caused partial outputs to leak across cursors. This PR unifies header interpretation for project/org keys, formalizes scoped token handling and request signing/nonce headers, ensures CORS preflight exposes the necessary headers, and moves auth checks earlier in the streaming pipeline. It also includes small OpenAI-compat adapter changes so existing clients sending OpenAI organization headers continue to work. Changes: 1) Canonical header precedence: Authorization Bearer token is primary; token prefixes are used to distinguish org vs project keys (org_*, proj_*). 2) Support for explicit project/org headers: X-Redwood-Project-Id and OpenAI-Organization are mapped to internal context with validation and fallbacks. 3) Scoped tokens: tokens may carry scope claims (e.g., "project:read", "project:write", "tool:invoke"); middleware enforces scope at route/tool-call boundaries and instruments detailed audit logs. 4) Request signing and nonce: New headers X-Redwood-Request-Signature and X-Redwood-Request-Nonce introduced for short-lived signed requests; server verifies signature and nonce freshness to mitigate replay. 5) CORS: preflight and response now include Access-Control-Expose-Headers for X-Redwood-Request-Nonce and X-Redwood-Request-Signature and allow credentials where applicable for browser-based project-scoped keys. 6) Streaming stability: auth and scope enforcement move to pre-stream handshake; streams now attach a minimal auth context to chunk metadata; token revocation is checked on stream resume and the stream is terminated cleanly if auth fails. 7) Tool/function calling: when the runtime invokes an external tool, the original request's scope and provenance are forwarded as masked metadata and the tool-call path validates required scopes before invocation. 8) OpenAI compatibility adapter: maps Authorization and OpenAI-Organization to new internal headers and maintains backwards-compatible behavior. Migration notes: Most clients will not need changes if they continue to send Authorization: Bearer <token>. Clients relying on X-Project or custom header behaviors should switch to X-Redwood-Project-Id or send a scoped token. See docs/openai-compat/auth.md for details and examples. Tests: unit tests added for header precedence, nonce verification, scoped token enforcement; integration tests added for streaming handshake and tool-call auth. Rollout: feature flag gated for one release to monitor for regressions; telemetry added for header usage and sign/nonce failures.

review_comments: Liam: Overall looks good. Please add a migration note for customers using custom proxy headers and a short explanation of token prefix strategy.
Ava: Added docs/openai-compat/auth.md and a brief section in CHANGELOG. Token prefix strategy documented under 'Token formats' in the doc.
Priya: Need an e2e test for browser-based CORS with credentials and project-scoped keys. Also confirm that Access-Control-Expose-Headers works when using signed requests.
Ava: Added e2e test and updated CORS middleware to always include the expose headers list when credentials are enabled. Added integration test to CI pipeline.
Ethan: Security review: ensure nonces are stored in TTL cache and rate-limited to avoid DoS. Also add telemetry for nonce verification failures.
Ava: Implemented nonce TTL cache and added counters and histograms for signature/nonce verifications. Security scan re-run and passed.
release_notes: Unify auth header semantics: Authorization token prefixes distinguish org vs project keys; X-Redwood-Project-Id and OpenAI-Organization mapping; Scoped tokens enforced for tool calls and APIs; New request signing headers (X-Redwood-Request-Signature, X-Redwood-Request-Nonce) with replay protection; CORS now exposes signing/nonce headers; Streaming auth handshake moved earlier to prevent partial output leakage; Backwards-compatible for Authorization Bearer users. See docs/openai-compat/auth.md for migration steps.
notes_for_ops: Feature gated behind 'auth.header_unify' flag. Monitor telemetry key 'auth.header.usage' and 'auth.signature.failures'. Roll out to 10% audience first. If nonce verification errors increase >5% baseline, rollback the flag and investigate.
